skills.observableOutcome: Counts groups of up to five objects using one-to-one correspondence.
Recognizes common two-dimensional shapes by their visible attributes.
Recognizes that plants need water and sunlight to grow.
Identifies the initial sound in familiar English words.
Identifies the first sound in familiar spoken English words.
Recognizes familiar words that share the same ending sound.
Understands and selects familiar English words in everyday contexts.
Counts pictured objects accurately using one-to-one correspondence.
Recognizes and continues simple number and visual patterns.
Solves simple joining and separating problems using quantities.
Recognizes common two-dimensional shapes and their visible properties.
Identifies age-appropriate facts about familiar living things and the surrounding world.
Follows a short spoken instruction and identifies a directly stated detail in a familiar context.
Orders a short familiar story or event sequence using pictures and simple language.
Observes a familiar living thing or object and makes a simple prediction linked to visible evidence.
Uses controlled marks and early letter-like forms with age-appropriate pencil and hand control.
Represents an idea using a simple, guided art or construction activity.
Practises taking turns, sharing materials and cooperating during a familiar activity.
Uses a simple strategy to pause, listen, and return to a learning task after a challenge.
Compares two familiar objects by a visible attribute such as length, height or size.
Describes a simple observable feature of daily weather.
Identifies a safe, age-appropriate action that helps care for a familiar environment.
Identifies familiar living and non-living things and describes one visible feature of the world around them.

activities.prompt: A ribbon is 5 blocks long. A string is 3 blocks long. How many blocks longer is the ribbon?
activities.feedbackCorrect: Well done! Five blocks is two more than three blocks.
activities.feedbackIncorrect: Count on from 3 to 5 to find the difference.

optionRationales.a: One block is not the difference between five and three.
optionRationales.b: Five is two more than three.
optionRationales.c: Three is the length of the shorter object, not the difference.

optionRationales.b: Six cups is more than four cups.

activities.prompt: A pencil is 8 cubes long. A crayon is 5 cubes long. A ruler is 10 cubes long. Which is the shortest?

optionRationales.b: Five cubes is the shortest measurement.
optionRationales.c: Ten cubes is the longest measurement.

guidedTasks.title: Make careful lines and shapes
instructions: Sit comfortably and hold the pencil gently with an adult's help.
Trace a short straight line, a curved line and a circle.
Draw one shape of your choice.
observableCriteria: Uses a comfortable grip with support as needed
Attempts a recognisable line or shape
guidedTasks.assessment: Adult observation; no fixed right/wrong answer.

guidedTasks.title: Create a picture of a place you know
instructions: Choose a familiar place such as a garden or home.
Draw at least two things you can see there.
Tell an adult one thing about your picture.
observableCriteria: Represents an idea using marks or shapes
Communicates one idea about the work
guidedTasks.assessment: Adult observation; accept varied creative responses.

guidedTasks.title: Build together and take turns
instructions: Choose blocks or safe building pieces with an adult.
Take turns adding one piece at a time.
observableCriteria: Waits for a turn with support
guidedTasks.assessment: Adult observation; do not compare siblings or score speed.

guidedTasks.title: Pause, breathe and try again
instructions: When a task feels difficult, pause your hands.
Take one slow breath with an adult.
Listen to the next small step and try again.
observableCriteria: Returns to the task with support
guidedTasks.assessment: Adult observation; supportive practice, never a penalty.

guidedTasks.title: Observe a plant safely
instructions: With an adult, choose a plant you can see from a safe place. Do not pick, taste or touch unknown plants.
Look at a leaf, stem or flower and notice its colour or shape.
Draw what you see or tell the adult one thing you noticed.
observableCriteria: Observes the plant safely without damaging it
Describes one visible feature such as colour or shape
Records the observation through a drawing or spoken description
guidedTasks.assessment: Adult observation; no fixed right/wrong answer. Never taste or handle an unknown plant.

guidedTasks.title: Put plant growth pictures in order
instructions: Ask an adult to show three picture cards: a seed, a sprout and a young plant.
Arrange the cards in the order they happen: first, next and last.
Tell the adult one thing that changes as the plant grows.
observableCriteria: Places the three growth stages in a sensible order
Uses first, next and last to describe the sequence
Describes one simple change as the plant grows
guidedTasks.assessment: Adult observation; accept spoken, drawn or arranged-card responses without scoring.
